findings.affected_surface: CLI usage/error message on unrecognized subcommand
findings.old_behavior: When an unrecognized subcommand is given, the error message displays: usage: git-gui [{blame|browser|citool}]
findings.new_behavior: When an unrecognized subcommand is given, the error message now displays: usage: git-gui [{blame|browser|citool|gui|pick}]
findings.compatibility_reason: The user-visible error/usage message format has changed. Any wrapper script, integration test, or documentation that parses or matches the exact usage string will see a different output. While the semantic behavior (exit code 1, error output) is preserved, the exact text has changed.
findings.why_not_internal_only: The usage/error message is displayed to end users via stderr or tk_messageBox when an invalid subcommand is provided. It is a user-visible output format change that any consumer of git-gui output could observe.
findings.uncertainty: Low. The change is a trivial text update adding two subcommand names. The old and new text are both definitively known from the diff.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that no downstream wrapper scripts, CI pipelines, or documentation match the exact usage string text.
findings.test_recommendation: Invoke git-gui with an invalid subcommand (e.g., 'git gui bogus') and verify that (a) the usage message contains the new subcommand list, (b) exit code remains 1, and (c) the error is still delivered via the same channel (stderr on non-Win32, tk_messageBox on Win32).
